recentEventsByGoal.objective:
=== Goal ===
Objective: Produce a source-grounded Phase-2 reuse assessment for Kepler’s earliest legitimate prerequisites—P1 causal market observations, P4 trustworthy evaluation, and minimal P3 sequential long/short/flat decisions—identifying the smallest real gaps and a non-implementing next research slice.
Success criteria: Deliver (A) a capability matrix for all three problems with minimum functional need, existing Kepler capability, candidate solution, REUSE/ADAPT/BUILD/DEFER classification, citations, and uncertainty; (B) evidence-supported blockers separated from inconveniences, unknowns, and unnecessary features; (C) no more than 2–3 realistic approaches per problem with tradeoffs and no unsupported ranking; (D) cheapest targeted experiments for uncertain/adapted capabilities, each with question, setup, expected observation, and rejection criterion; and (E) explicit answers on immediate reuse, adaptation, justified builds, deferrals, and the smallest next vertical research slice. Cite exact repository and installed Qlib/RD-Agent files/classes/functions and dated upstream docs/source or other primary evidence where applicable. For every BUILD, state the observed blocker to REUSE/ADAPT; otherwise do not classify it BUILD. Mark claims KNOWN, LIKELY, UNKNOWN — TARGETED EXPERIMENT REQUIRED, or UNKNOWN — TARGETED RESEARCH REQUIRED.
Boundaries: Investigate only P1, P4, and minimal P3 and the user’s special investigation questions. Inspect the repository and installed dependencies; use targeted upstream and external research as needed. Do not implement experiments or the slice, change code, design the full Kepler architecture or future data stack, optimize a strategy, or add common trading-system components without demonstrated need.
Constraints: Derive data and mechanical requirements from first useful research questions and accurate simulation of chosen perpetual instruments; do not preselect instrument count, history length, bar frequency, fields, leverage/risk rules, stops, position count, optimizer, or a custom solution. Evaluate Qlib first, then RD-Agent, official exchange/data APIs, mature open-source tools, established methods, and only then custom work. Distinguish crypto-perpetual support, integration fit, assumptions, and maintenance cost from mere feature presence or popularity. Keep uncertainty as uncertainty rather than an architecture decision.
If blocked: Stop and ask the user when access to necessary repository/package/source evidence or an essential research-use-case choice prevents a supported conclusion; otherwise label unresolved claims and propose targeted research/experiments rather than guessing.
